Tip diversification rates (DR) of Jetz et al. (2012)

Source: R/dr_rates.R
dr_rates.Rd

dr_rates() computes the DR statistic of Jetz et al. (2012), a measure of the recent rate of speciation of each tip from the tree alone: the inverse of its equal-splits measure of evolutionary distinctiveness, DR_i = 1 / sum_j l_j / 2^(j - 1), where l_j is the length of the j-th edge on the path from tip i to the root, the terminal edge first. Tips in recently and rapidly diversifying clades have short, heavily shared paths and a high DR.

Usage

dr_rates(tree, per = c("tip", "edge"))

Arguments

tree

A rooted phylo tree with branch lengths.

per

"tip" for one value per tip, named by the tips, or "edge" for one value per edge, in the order of tree$edge.

Value

A numeric vector of DR values.

Details

With per = "edge", each edge gets the geometric mean of the DR of the tips below it (the DR of its tip for a terminal edge), a value per edge in the order of tree$edge that can be given as the edge_covariate of damocles_fit() or damocles_samples(). DR is defined for tips; the value of an internal edge summarises its descendants and is not an estimate of the rate along that edge, unlike the branch-specific rates of model-based methods such as ClaDS. data-raw/damocles_clads.R checks the tip values against the equal-splits measure of picante::evol.distinct() and compares DR with ClaDS as covariates.

References

Jetz, W., Thomas, G. H., Joy, J. B., Hartmann, K., & Mooers, A. O. (2012). The global diversity of birds in space and time. Nature, 491, 444–448. doi:10.1038/nature11631

See also

damocles_fit(), damocles_samples().

Examples

set.seed(10)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(20)
head(dr_rates(tr))
#>       t1       t2       t3       t4       t5       t6 
#> 2.227964 2.227964 1.436217 2.056434 2.056434 1.163367 
head(dr_rates(tr, per = "edge"))
#> [1] 1.924622 2.227964 2.227964 2.227964 1.436217 2.768076
